stories.stat_label: wild seahorse filmed in Irish waters
stories.headline: Night divers filmed a rare seahorse in Ireland's seagrass
stories.summary: A long-snouted seahorse just 4-5 cm long was spotted in Cork seagrass. Ireland has only 8 earlier records, most over 100 years old, the latest live one in 1956.
stories.why: It's believed to be the 1st time a wild seahorse has been caught on video in Irish waters.

stories.stat_label: years old: the earliest known dice
stories.headline: Native Americans were rolling dice 12,800 years ago
stories.summary: Two-sided bone dice from Ice Age sites predate the oldest Old World dice by 6,000+ years. A researcher identified 600+ dice at 57 sites across 12 US states.
stories.why: It means games of chance, an early step toward probability, began in the Americas.

stories.headline: Coconut waste fuel ran a jet engine as well as kerosene
stories.summary: Osaka chemists turned discarded coconut into jet fuel at low heat. Blended up to 50% with kerosene, it matched kerosene's efficiency and cut unburned hydrocarbons by 5-40%.
stories.why: They say it's the 1st time coconut biofuel has been tested in a jet engine.

stories.stat_label: until rare doves had eggs again
stories.headline: Rats and pigs are gone, and a Samoan island is blooming
stories.summary: After 12 expeditions and 130+ days removing invasive rats and pigs, seedlings now carpet the forest. A month later, rare shy ground doves were nesting with eggs.
stories.why: A land crab never recorded there before turned up, and locals can grow taro again.

fun_fact: The ancient dice were 2-sided, like a coin: one marked face counted as the scoring side.
